text: 🇲🇽✊ "No luxuries, no privileges for rulers. The presidential plane was sold — and the sale built two hospitals." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tuxtepec, Oaxaca Sheinbaum supervised the new IMSS Bienestar General Hospital in Tuxtepec, one of two hospitals funded by the sale of the presidential plane (the other is in Tlapa, Guerrero). Investment: 2.3 billion pesos; 150 beds; it will serve 1.2 million people in 109 municipalities of Oaxaca and Veracruz. Inauguration is set for August 4. She also announced 3 billion pesos to fix every operating room, hospital and clinic in Oaxaca.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>NEARSHORING IS LANDING: PLANT OPENINGS TRIPLE</u>

The nearshoring obituary was premature. New investment announcements fell nearly 80% in Q1 2026 as boardrooms wait out the T-MEC review — but inaugurations of previously committed plants are running at almost triple last year’s pace, Integralia analyst Alberto Quiroz told El Economista.

The corridor is clear: Querétaro and Guanajuato, up through San Luis Potosí to Nuevo León and Coahuila. Airbus opened a $35.8M plant in Querétaro, Clarios a $147M distribution center in Torreón, and Baltimore Aircoil its first Latin American factory in Nuevo León — $100M, 500 direct jobs.

The capital that was promised is arriving.

🇲🇽⚓ <u>211 NEW NAVAL OFFICERS — RECORD 73 WOMEN — SWORN TO DEFEND SOVEREIGNTY</u>

President Sheinbaum presided over the graduation of 211 naval engineer officers at the Heroica Escuela Naval Militar in Alvarado, Veracruz — the 2022-2026 class, with a record 73 women among them.

"Mexico believes in you, Mexico trusts in you, Mexico knows that when it needs you, you will be there — as the sailors of our homeland have always been," she told the new guardiamarinas, who carry "the responsibility of defending sovereignty, protecting Mexicans and honoring the homeland with values."

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>NINE CITIES MARCH AGAINST CHIHUAHUA’S WATER DEAL WITH ISRAEL</u>

Marches in at least nine Mexican cities — Chihuahua, Ciudad Juárez, Mexico City, Puebla, Aguascalientes, Saltillo, Pachuca, Toluca, Monterrey, Querétaro — demanded the cancellation of the water cooperation deal between Chihuahua’s water utility (JCAS) and Mashav, the Israeli Foreign Ministry’s cooperation agency, signed in February 2023 and in force until 2027.

Organizers Salvemos los Cerros and Asamblea Feminista accused PAN governor Maru Campos of promoting Zionism as "a colonial political project" and doing business with a government committing genocide in Gaza. Protesters also demanded a ceasefire and the end of Mexico-Israel diplomatic and trade ties. In Puebla, police blocked 150 marchers from reaching the Zócalo.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>ARMY CAPTURES CARTEL BOSS WITH $5M US BOUNTY</u>

Federal forces led by the Mexican Army captured Alfonso "N," alias "Poncho La Quiringua" — head of the Los Reyes cartel — in Imbarácuaro, Michoacán, with two artillery helicopters backing the operation. He had an arrest warrant for kidnapping and riot, and Washington was offering $5 million for him; he is linked to the 2025 drone attacks on soldiers in Cotija, Tingüindín and Jacona, and identified as a close collaborator of "El Abuelo" Farías.

The cartel answered with five narco-blockades and torched vehicles in Los Reyes and Peribán. Under control within hours, Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch reported.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>NEARSHORING KEEPS LANDING: PLANT INAUGURATIONS TRIPLE IN MEXICO</u>

Yes, new investment announcements fell nearly 80% in the first quarter as companies wait out the T-MEC review. But the money committed in previous years is turning into steel and jobs: "In inaugurations we're seeing almost triple what we saw last year," Integralia analyst Alberto Quiroz told El Economista.

The evidence runs along the Bajío-to-border corridor: Airbus opened a $35.8 million plant in Colón, Querétaro; Clarios a $147 million automated center in Torreón moving 11 million batteries a year; Baltimore Aircoil its first Latin America plant in Nuevo León ($100 million, 500 jobs); China's Zoomlion its Latin American agri-machinery hub in Aguascalientes.

Announcements are headlines. Inaugurations are production.

🇲🇽⚓ <u>"MEXICO BELIEVES IN YOU, MEXICO TRUSTS YOU": SHEINBAUM TO 211 NEW NAVY OFFICERS</u>

President Claudia Sheinbaum presided over the graduation of 211 guardiamarinas of the Heroica Escuela Naval Militar in Alvarado, Veracruz — 170 fleet officers, 27 marines and 14 naval pilots, including a record 73 women, the most ever to graduate from the institution.

"Mexico believes in you, Mexico trusts you, Mexico knows that when it needs you, you will be there — as the sailors of our homeland have always been," the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces told them. "You carry on your shoulders the responsibility of defending sovereignty."

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>MEXICANS MARCH AGAINST PAN GOVERNOR'S WATER DEAL WITH ISRAEL</u>

From Chihuahua and Ciudad Juárez to the Ángel de la Independencia in Mexico City, protesters demanded the cancellation of the water cooperation deal between Chihuahua's water board and Mashav — Israel's state cooperation agency — signed in 2023, valid until 2027 and never registered with Mexico's Foreign Ministry.

Marches also hit Puebla, Monterrey, Saltillo, Pachuca, Toluca, Aguascalientes and Querétaro, with demands for a Gaza ceasefire and an end to commercial ties with Israel.

"Who decides over Chihuahua's water, and under what interests?" asked Salvemos los Cerros, accusing PAN governor Maru Campos of doing business with a government committing genocide.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MICHOACÁN: ARMY TAKES DOWN CARTEL BOSS THE U.S. HAD A $5M BOUNTY ON</u>

Mexico's Army detained Alfonso "Poncho La Quiringua" Fernández Magallón, boss of the Cártel de Los Reyes, in Imbarácuaro, Michoacán — a man U.S. authorities offered up to $5 million for, accused of drone attacks on Mexican soldiers in Cotija, Tingüindín and Jacona.

The cartel's answer was five roadblocks and burning vehicles in Los Reyes and Peribán. Security forces had them cleared within five hours. He now sits in FGR facilities in Mexico City.

Mexican intelligence, Mexican operation, Mexican results.
